    Parsley 0.1.1-SNAPSHOT API

    Parsley is a Java library that provides causal delivery order for Kafka Streams processors. When the required conditions are met, every wrapped processor processes records in causal order, even when records originate from multiple topics and partitions. It does this by encoding each message's causal dependencies onto the message and buffering records until those dependencies have been observed.

    The entire public surface lives in a single package, io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley. It consists of interfaces and value types. Every implementation is package-private and obtained through a static factory: ParsleyProcessors, CausalStreams, and CausalDependencies.

    There are two entry points into the causal guarantee. ParsleyProcessors is the low-level decorator: it wraps one user Processor and you wire it into a topology you build and own yourself. CausalStreams is the high-level, topology-owning builder: it composes the same decorator internally, but owns the surrounding sources, processor, and sinks itself, which unlocks guarantees the decorator alone cannot provide — a sink partitioner applied uniformly across every sink, co-partitioning validation that covers sinks as well as inputs, and coordinated graceful shutdown via ParsleyQuiesce.

    A running topology can also evolve — add a stage, replace a stage, recompile — across a leaderless epoch boundary coordinated by ParsleyCoordination, so a new node adopts the current causal floor instead of replaying pre-epoch history into the shared frontier. It is optional; without it a topology runs in epoch 0, unchanged.

    Core concepts

    Causal dependencies
    The positions a consumer must have observed before a record stamped with them may be delivered. They are a producer's snapshot of what it had seen when it sent the record. They are carried as CausalDependencies in a parsley-causal-dependencies header. Build one from a consumed record by starting with using to bind a topic resolver, then folding in each record with observe. Combine several for a fan-in with merge, and attach the result to an outbound record with stamp. When consuming a topic a Parsley topology produces, fold every record in with observe but skip those for which isWatermark returns true, which are protocol metadata rather than business records.
    Causal frontier
    The highest offset a causal processor has contiguously admitted on each topic-partition. It is never a coordinate the processor merely happens to have seen something later on, because a later-offset record may be forwarded before an earlier one that is still held on the same partition. The frontier is keyed by topic UUID, so topic deletion and recreation produce a distinct identity even when the name is reused. A record is delivered once every input channel has confirmed every coordinate the record depends on (the per-coordinate minimum across all input channels). The frontier is internal to ParsleyProcessors and is not a separate public type.
    Protocol watermark
    A record with a null value, keyed with the triggering record's key, marked with a _parsley_watermark header, that carries a node's completeness frontier downstream when a delivered input produced no business output. Reusing the key routes it to the same partition the record's output would. It keeps causal progress flowing through filters and not-yet-emitting aggregates. Parsley's processors handle watermarks internally; a plain Kafka client detects them with isWatermark.
    Causal buffer
    Records whose dependencies are not yet satisfied are held in a changelog-backed buffer and released as soon as the frontier catches up. A
    invalid reference 
    io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalBufferLimit
    bounds how long or how large the buffer may grow. When the limit fires before a held record's dependencies are satisfied, the outcome is governed by the parsley.buffer.eviction.failure.policy configuration. By default Parsley fails the task and leaves the record buffered for retry, which keeps delivery in causal order. Setting the policy to continue forwards the held record out of causal order instead. Parsley never drops or diverts a record under either policy, and every firing is logged and counted.

    Entry points

    TypePurpose
    io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.ParsleyProcessorSupplier<KIn,VIn,KOut,VOut>Wraps a user Kafka Streams Processor so that its state access and its forward calls run behind the causal guarantee. It is built through ParsleyProcessors.
    CausalStreamsThe topology-owning builder: composes ParsleyProcessors internally and owns the sources, processor, and sinks around it, so it can apply a uniform sink partitioner and validate co-partitioning across sinks as well as inputs.
    ParsleyQuiesceA shared handle for coordinating graceful shutdown across every causal task in one application instance. Register it via withQuiesce on either builder; call requestQuiesce() and poll isSafeToClose() before closing KafkaStreams.
    ParsleyCoordinationA shared, leaderless handle for evolving a running topology across an epoch boundary, so a new or replaced stage adopts the current causal floor rather than replaying pre-epoch history into the shared frontier. Register it via withCoordination on either builder; call requestEpochTransition() to evolve, and close() in shutdown. Optional — without it a topology runs in epoch 0.
    CausalDependenciesStamps and reads causal dependencies directly on plain ProducerRecord and ConsumerRecord objects, for talking to a Parsley topology from outside Kafka Streams.
    CausalAuditOptional callback interface supplied to the builder via withAudit. Receives per-record buffering events — forwarded, held, released, evicted, and deserialization failures — carrying record identity and causal metadata only, never the record payload.

    Typical usage

    
// Low-level: inside a Kafka Streams topology you build and own
builder.stream(List.of("prices", "orders"), Consumed.with(Serdes.String(), orderSerde))
       .process(ParsleyProcessors.builder(userSupplier)
               .addBufferStore("parsley", CausalBufferLimit.ofDuration(limit))
               .addBuffer(ParsleyBuffer.of("prices", Serdes.String(), priceSerde))
               .addBuffer(ParsleyBuffer.of("orders", Serdes.String(), orderSerde))
               .build())
       .to("output-topic");

// High-level: CausalStreams owns the topology itself
Topology topology = CausalStreams.builder(userSupplier)
        .addBufferStore("parsley", CausalBufferLimit.ofDuration(limit))
        .addSource(ParsleyBuffer.of("prices", Serdes.String(), priceSerde))
        .addSource(ParsleyBuffer.of("orders", Serdes.String(), orderSerde))
        .addSink("enriched-sink", "enriched-output", Serdes.String(), enrichedSerde)
        .build();
new KafkaStreams(topology, props).start();

// At the edge, from a plain Kafka client
CausalDependencies deps = CausalDependencies.using(topics).observe(consumedRecord);
producer.send(deps.stamp(new ProducerRecord<>("orders", key, value)));
